description: Phase 1, the highest-confidence model-agnostic win (jev cut protocol calls 1092 -> 101 mostly here). Adopt jev's browser-loop MECHANICS in TypeScript/Playwright: (a) an ATOMIC single-call fast snapshot returning a persistent in-page node-identity map + per-node semantic guards + a page-level marker in ONE page.evaluate; (b) execution that acts on the OBSERVED node WITHOUT a fresh locator query, via a window-scoped identity map (like jev's window.__jevFast); (c) a per-node freshness re-check (guard + pageKey for click/select, whole-page marker otherwise) plus a pre-input occlusion/geometry hit-test (elementFromPoint) that rejects covered/off-viewport controls BEFORE input; (d) an adaptive event-driven wait (wait for the expected autocomplete options up to fastWaitCapMs, else a couple animation frames) replacing the fixed wait on the hot path. ALL behind the LAYA_FAST_LOOP flag (default OFF) so main's behavior and the green suite are untouched. Guard the untrusted in-page-eval boundary: validate the identity map / guard / marker structures returned from page.evaluate before trusting them.
steps: In src/snapshot.ts: add `export async function captureFast(page: Page, options?: CaptureOptions): Promise<FastSnapshot>`. It runs ONE self-contained in-page function (like domWalk, closing over nothing from Node) that: initializes/reuses a window-scoped identity cache `window.__layaFast = { ids: new WeakMap(), nodes: new Map(), next: 1 }` and prunes entries whose node is not isConnected (mirror jev snapshot.js); assigns each selected visible interactive element a persistent integer nodeId via the WeakMap; ALSO stamps data-laya-ref=eN in DOM order (so resolveRef still works and the legacy path is unaffected); for each control computes the NodeGuard (role, accessible name, value, checked, selectedIndex, disabled, aria-expanded/checked/selected, href, and scopeText = nearest form/dialog/[role=dialog]/article/li/tr/[role=row] innerText sliced to ~6000 chars) and its viewport rect {x,y,w,h}; computes a page-level `marker` string = JSON of [href, scroll, viewport, title, visibleText, and the per-node semantic tuples] and a `pageKey` string = JSON of [href, scroll, viewport, and every input/textarea/select node's [id,value,checked,selectedIndex,disabled,readOnly]] (both mirroring jev). Return { url, title, visibleText, controls (FastControl[] with nodeId/guard/rect), text, pageKey, marker }. Reuse the existing accessibleName/roleFor/isEditable/isVisibleWithRect helpers where possible (extract shared logic rather than duplicating; keep domWalk behavior byte-identical). VALIDATE the returned object at the Node boundary: assert it is an object with string url/title/visibleText/text/pageKey/marker and an array of controls each with a finite integer nodeId, a well-formed guard, and a numeric rect; on any malformed field, THROW a clear error (the fast path must never trust unvalidated eval output). Add a small `isFastSnapshot`-style validator.

In src/browser.ts: add persistent-identity execution + freshness to BrowserSession. (a) `async resolveByNodeId(page, nodeId): Locator` - returns a locator that targets the exact observed node via an in-page hook: expose a helper the page installs (e.g. window.__layaFast.nodes) and resolve by tagging that node with a fresh unique attribute inside one evaluate then locating it, OR use page.evaluateHandle to get the ElementHandle from window.__layaFast.nodes.get(nodeId) and act on the handle. Prefer the ElementHandle approach so NO selector re-query/DOM re-walk happens (this is the round-trip win). (b) `async freshGuard(page, nodeId, expectedGuard: NodeGuard, expectedPageKey: string, wholePageMarker?: {expected:string}): Promise<boolean>` - for a targeted click/select, re-evaluate [pageKey, guard(nodeId)] in ONE call and deep-equal it to [expectedPageKey, expectedGuard]; for non-targeted freshness, compare the whole-page marker. Return false (stale) on any mismatch or when the node is gone. (c) `async actOnNode(page, nodeId, kind: 'click'|'fill'|'select', opts): Promise<{ok:true}|{ok:false, reason:'stale'|'covered'|'gone'}>` - in ONE evaluate resolve the node from window.__layaFast.nodes, re-check isConnected/visible/enabled/not-readonly-for-fill, compute center (x,y) from getBoundingClientRect, and OCCLUSION hit-test `e.contains(document.elementFromPoint(x,y))` (reject covered controls, matching jev.act); only then perform the input (for fill: focus+selectAll+type the text; for select: set value + dispatch input/change; for click: click at center). Return a structured result so the loop can re-observe on stale/covered rather than throwing. Add a `SETTLE`-style bounded adaptive wait `async adaptiveWait(page, {node, kind, capMs}): Promise<void>` that, after a fill into a combobox, waits (via requestAnimationFrame loop inside one evaluate) for visible [role=option] under the field's aria-controls/aria-owns up to capMs, otherwise resolves after >=2 animation frames or a short floor (mirror jev observe's after_input wait). Guard EVERY evaluate defensively so a mid-navigation rejection degrades to 'stale'/'gone' instead of throwing.

In src/autopilot/loop.ts: thread a `fastLoop?: boolean` and `fastWaitCapMs?: number` through RunGoalOptions (default false / from config). When fastLoop is ON: capture via captureFast, build the numbered PageState from its controls (buildState already caps/renders - pass FastControl[] which are Control-compatible so buildState and the engine are unchanged; keep nodeId/guard/rect on a side map keyed by ref so the decision layer still uses refs), and in execute() for CLICK/TYPE_TEXT/SELECT/FILL_FORM use the persistent-identity path: freshGuard-check the target's guard+pageKey captured at decision time; if stale/covered, re-capture and re-decide (bounded, reuse the existing self-heal retry budget) instead of blindly re-querying; act via actOnNode (no fresh locator query); then adaptiveWait instead of the fixed post-action settle on the hot path. When fastLoop is OFF, the code path is EXACTLY as today (capture()/resolveRef()/locate()/probeSettle()); do not alter the default path. Keep the change additive and small; put the fast-path branch behind one clear conditional.

In src/server.ts: thread config.fastLoop and config.fastWaitCapMs into the runGoal options where the other config flags are threaded (so LAYA_FAST_LOOP actually reaches the loop in production). Grep for where snapshotBackend / viewportPriority / settleProbe are passed and add the two new options alongside.

Add behavioral tests in a new test/fast-loop.test.ts (real headless Chromium, following the fixture pattern in test/autopilot*.test.ts and test/snapshot.test.ts). Cover, with assertions that FAIL if the fast-path behavior regresses: (1) captureFast returns a persistent nodeId that is STABLE for the same element across two captures on an unchanged page, and CHANGES/prunes when the element is removed; (2) captureFast returns a well-formed guard + pageKey + marker and the validator rejects a malformed structure; (3) freshGuard returns true on an unchanged target and false after the target's value/label/scope mutates or the node detaches; (4) actOnNode refuses a control that is fully COVERED by an overlay (occlusion hit-test) with reason 'covered', and succeeds once the overlay is removed; (5) an end-to-end runGoal with LAYA_FAST_LOOP on (via option) + StubEngine drives a real fixture form to its independent final-page verified success in FEWER browser round-trips than the same run with the flag off (assert a measurable reduction, e.g. count captures/locator queries via a small instrumentation hook or by asserting the fast path took the actOnNode branch and not resolveRef). Build a tiny local fixture (an overlay-covered button; a combobox with delayed autocomplete options) if the existing fixtures do not cover occlusion/autocomplete.

Run pnpm run typecheck, pnpm run build, pnpm test. Confirm the DEFAULT suite is unchanged (same pass/skip counts as FEAT-001 baseline) and the new fast-loop tests pass. Confirm behavior parity: a fixture run with the flag OFF and ON reaches the SAME verified final-page outcome.
acceptance_criteria: captureFast performs exactly ONE page.evaluate for the whole snapshot (identity + controls + guards + marker + pageKey), verified by test/instrumentation.
With LAYA_FAST_LOOP on, a targeted action resolves and acts on the observed node WITHOUT a fresh selector re-query (actOnNode path taken; asserted).
freshGuard correctly reports fresh vs stale for click/select targets and marker for whole-page freshness (asserted).
actOnNode rejects an occluded/covered control before input and succeeds when uncovered (asserted).
The in-page-eval result is validated at the Node boundary; a malformed structure throws a clear error (asserted).
With the flag OFF, the default suite pass/skip counts are identical to the FEAT-001 baseline (no behavior change on main's default path).
A fixture goal run reaches the SAME independently-verified final-page success with the flag ON as with it OFF, in fewer or equal browser round-trips (measured reduction shown).
No em dashes in any new comment/doc/test string; src/types.ts stays pure.
verification: Run `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run build`; both exit 0.
Run `pnpm test` and confirm the default suite matches the FEAT-001 baseline counts plus the new fast-loop tests, all green.
Run `pnpm vitest run test/fast-loop.test.ts` and confirm the persistent-identity, freshness-guard, occlusion, validation, and round-trip-reduction assertions pass.
Confirm behavioral parity: the same fixture goal verifies success with the flag ON and OFF.
